title: The blockers field has no CLI write path -- every Blocked task's reason is unrecorded and unverifiable
description:
Reported inbound by lore-cli via the orchestrator (opum-agent): lore-cli needed to move LCLI-333 to Blocked and name four opum-cli-e2e task ids as its blockers. It could set the status (quest task pause, the only path to Blocked), but found no CLI write path for the blockers field, confirmed against the full quest manifest, not just --help. It fell back to an unstructured task note.

Independently verified in this repo: quest manifest --json has zero mentions of 'blocker' anywhere; src/cli/main.ts, command-contract.ts, and command-help.ts have zero blocker-related flags or wiring; even the Backlog migration importer (backlog-public.ts:246) hardcodes blockers: [] rather than populating it from anything. The domain layer fully supports blocker events (BlockerEvent, activeBlockers(), opened/cleared semantics with reason/evidence validation -- blocker_duplicate_open, blocker_unknown_or_repeat_clear, blocker_clear_requires_evidence are all real, tested domain errors) but nothing in the CLI, manifest, or migration path ever reaches it. The field is displayed by task view (confirmed: quest task view <id> --json always shows blockers: []) and is real schema, not dead code -- so it reads as data to anyone who looks, and is silently always empty.

Why this matters beyond one workaround: this morning QCLI-196 was closed partly on the reasoning that a Blocked status with an empty blockers array, alongside five Done children, indicated a stale migration artifact. The orchestrator flagged the correction: the empty array was never evidence of anything, since nothing can write it -- every Blocked task in every Quest workspace has an empty blockers array by construction. It happened not to change QCLI-196's outcome because the five Done children were independent evidence, but the same inference on a task without such children would be unverifiable. See QCLI-196's notes for the caveat recorded there.

This is two-sided: (1) a schema field that exists, is displayed, and cannot be written by any command; (2) Blocked is therefore a status with no machine-readable reason attached, fleet-wide -- the reason always lives in prose, if recorded at all.

Design question for whoever scopes this (per the orchestrator, worth deciding before implementation): should blockers become writable, or should the field be removed in favor of the dependency edges that already work? lore-cli hit the other half of the same problem while filing this: a cross-repo task id (e.g. an opum-cli-e2e task id from lore-cli's workspace) cannot be expressed as a same-workspace dependency edge, so a working blockers field may be the only way to express 'blocked on another repository's task' -- which argues for making it writable rather than dropping it, if that cross-repo case is a real requirement.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A design decision is recorded first: blockers becomes writable via CLI flags (open/clear, with reason/evidence per the existing domain validation), or the field is removed from the schema in favor of dependency edges -- and if writable, whether it needs to support a cross-repository task reference that a same-workspace --dependency cannot express

If made writable: quest task edit gains flags to open and clear a blocker with the same actor-attribution and validation the domain layer already enforces (reason required to open, reason or evidence required to clear), and quest manifest / --help reflect the new flags
If made writable: a Blocked task's blockers array is populated and machine-readable, so a later reader (or QCLI-196's closure logic) does not have to re-derive intent from prose notes alone
Regression tests cover open/clear via the CLI and confirm the field round-trips through quest task view
